title.value: POMRL: No-Regret Learning-to-Plan with Increasing Horizons
title.justification: The title is directly extracted from the paper's heading, indicating a focus on planning under model uncertainty in a learning context.
title.quote: POMRL: No-Regret Learning-to-Plan with Increasing Horizons

extractions.description: This paper addresses planning under model uncertainty in an online meta-reinforcement learning setting, proposing an algorithm (POMRL) that meta-learns task relatedness to optimize planning horizons and reduce regret over a sequence of tasks. Theoretical findings and empirical validation highlight the benefits of adapting planning horizons based on accumulated task knowledge.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper focuses on a meta-reinforcement learning approach for optimizing planning in sequential tasks, with no direct mention of climate or ecological impacts.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: We study the problem of planning under model uncertainty in an online meta-reinforcement learning (RL) setting where an agent is presented with a sequence of related tasks.

primary_category.justification: The paper does not focus on a specific Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development theme but rather on a meta-reinforcement learning strategy for task-oriented planning.
primary_category.quote: The agent can use its experience in each task and across tasks to estimate both the transition model and the distribution over tasks.

primary_sub_category.justification: The sub-category list does not directly apply to this paper's focus on meta-reinforcement learning and task planning.
primary_sub_category.quote: We leverage this structural task similarity to obtain model estimators with faster convergence as more tasks are seen.

new_primary_category.justification: The content of the paper revolves around reinforcement learning and algorithm development without direct ties to sustainable development goals.
new_primary_category.quote: Our theoretical result highlights a new dependence of the planning horizon on the size of the within-task data m and on the number of tasks T.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: No new sub-category related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development can be derived from the paper, as its focus is strictly on reinforcement learning techniques.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: In this work, we consider a meta-reinforcement-learning problem made of a sequence of related tasks.
